title: Introduce jurisdictional denylist, KMS fallback rate-gate, and RBAC delegation limiter
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds jurisdictional denylist for operator interactions, KMS fallback rate-gate to prevent cross-region storms, and RBAC delegation limiter to reduce blast radius for delegated grants; rollout is gated and reversible.
commits: feat(auth): add jurisdictional denylist middleware and claim evaluator
feat(kms): implement fallback_rategate and provider selection heuristic
feat(rbac): add delegation limiter plumbing and metrics
chore(config): feature flag and defaults for jurisdictional denylist
docs: add operational runbook and migration notes
tests: integration tests for fallback behavior and denylist enforcement
description: Summary: Implement a production-safe enforcement mechanism to prevent operator or service actions against KMS-backed assets in forbidden jurisdictions, together with a conservative KMS fallback rate-gate and an RBAC delegation limiter to reduce cross-tenant escalation risk. Motivation: Several regulated customers and upcoming SOC audits requested stronger guarantees that operator actions (and accidental routing) cannot touch keys or tenant data outside approved geographies, and that KMS failovers cannot create traffic storms or unbounded cost/latency spikes. This PR adds three cooperating pieces: 1) Jurisdictional denylist middleware: evaluates operator claims and target resource region against a denylist configured per-organization and per-tenant. Denied attempts are routed to a new audit event (residency.denied) and return 403 with a machine-friendly error code. 2) KMS fallback rate-gate: when the primary KMS provider in the pinned region is unreachable, fallbacks are allowed but throttled per-tenant and per-region to a conservative default (10 requests/minute) with exponential backoff. Metrics emitted (kms.fallback.allowed, kms.fallback.rate_limited) plus tracing ensures visibility. 3) RBAC delegation limiter: caps automatic delegation operations (operator-created grants, token exchange flows) to a configurable global and per-operator rate to prevent blast radius from compromised operator credentials. Implementation notes: - A new OPA policy fragment (policy_compiler.go) compiles denylist checks into existing RBAC decision flow; we keep the decision path minimal to avoid p99 impact by short-circuiting on common allow paths. - middleware/jurisdictional_denylist.go is inserted into operator-auth chain before policy evaluation so audit events capture both the attempted action and the denial reason. - delegation_limiter.go is a leaky-bucket limiter backed by Redis with tenant isolation. Defaults live in config/defaults.yaml and are feature-gated behind jur_disallow_v2 and kms_fallback_rategate feature flags. - fallback_rategate.go implements the heuristic for choosing alternative KMS providers and enforces rate limits; it is pluggable into the KMS provider manager. - scripts/migrations/20241105_backfill_jurisdictional_claims.sql populates a lightweight claim table for tenants that previously set region pins via legacy fields (migration is a no-op for tenants already using the new attribute). Backwards compatibility and rollout: - This change is behind jur_disallow_v2 feature flag and coercive behavior is enabled only after staged rollout. Default is advisory mode (logs + audit events) for two weeks in canary regions (eu-west-1) before turning on enforcement. - We include a config toggle (jurisdictional.mode = advisory|enforce) to safely flip behavior in emergency. - Delegation limiter default is permissive during canary (500/min global, 50/min per-operator) and tightened after monitoring to safe defaults (100/min global, 10/min per-operator). Migration and operational steps: - Run the backfill migration during low-traffic windows. - Enable advisory mode in eu-west-1 for 2 weeks and monitor residency.denied and kms.fallback.rate_limited metrics. - After no customer regressions reported, flip to enforce for canary, then rollout region by region. - Ensure SRE runbook (docs/security/jurisdictional-denylist.md) is accessible to oncall for rollback steps (disable jur_disallow_v2 or set jurisdictional.mode=advisory). Testing: - Unit tests added for policy compiler branches and limiter logic. - Integration tests simulate KMS primary failover and verify fallback_rategate behavior and emitted metrics. - Load tests validate p99 latency impact is <5ms for auth path on canary. CI notes: - Initial integration job failed due to a race in the Redis limiter mock; fixed by adding deterministic seeding in tests. - Lint, unit, integration, and end-to-end suites pass on rerun. Review summary: - Anika requested stronger telemetry on denied decisions (added residency.denied.reason label and a trace span). - Miguel asked for explicit feature flag gating in k8s config (added entries to deployments/k8s/redwood-config.yaml). - Jonah requested a migration idempotence check (added check in SQL migration and test). Security review: - Threat model updated, no elevation path found; delegation limiter reduces risk significantly. - Audit logs now include both operator identity and resolved region claim for post-incident analysis. Merge: Squashed and merged after approvals from Anika and Miguel, and green CI.
review_comments: Anika Patel (reviewer): Please surface an explicit audit tag with the denial reason and include a tracing span so we can tie this to CI events later. -- Addressed by adding residency.denied.reason and trace span in middleware.

Miguel Santos (security reviewer): Make sure the k8s config exposes the feature flag so operators can toggle without deploy changes. Also include conservative defaults. -- Added flag to redwood-config.yaml and updated defaults.yaml.
Jonah Feldman (sre): Migration must be idempotent and safe to run multiple times. Add a uniqueness guard. -- Added idempotence check and unit test for the migration script.
